tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='crates/shep-core/src/config/app.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""    /// A whole number
    Int(i64),
""","""    /// A whole number that fits `i64`
    Int(i64),
    /// A whole number beyond `i64::MAX`, up to `u64::MAX`
    Uint(u64),
""")
s=s.replace("""            Self::Int(n) => n.to_string(),
""","""            Self::Int(n) => n.to_string(),
            Self::Uint(n) => n.to_string(),
""")
s=s.replace("""                // A u64 beyond i64::MAX is valid JSON; wrapping it would turn
                // it into a negative number.
                Ok(EnvValue::Int(
                    v.try_into().map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?,
                ))
""","""                Ok(EnvValue::Uint(v))
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cargo check -p shep-core; echo rc=$?

result_text:
Done: `cargo check -p shep-core` passes.

In `crates/shep-core/src/config/app.rs`, I added an `EnvValue::Uint(u64)` variant. `visit_u64` now stores into it instead of forcing the value into an `i64`, so every `u64` up to `u64::MAX` loads as its exact decimal digits. `into_string` handles the new arm. `visit_i64` is untouched, so negatives down to `i64::MIN` and the other value kinds load as before, and serialization still writes strings.

I only ran `cargo check`, as asked. I didn't run the tests, and I added none.
